text: Lucia stood in her noisy kitchen with a can of tomatoes in one hand and her phone in the other. The mixer was running, so she spoke loudly. "Hey phone, how long does it take to drive to my sister's house?" The phone said the drive was thirty minutes with light traffic. Lucia frowned. She planned to leave tonight after dinner, when the roads are busy. "Check it for tonight after dinner," she said. The assistant looked at the usual traffic for that hour and said the trip would take forty-five minutes. Then Lucia asked it to convert the distance from miles to kilometers, because her sister's car shows kilometers. The assistant said it was twenty-two miles, about thirty-five kilometers, and Lucia went back to her tomatoes.

Chiara sat at her desk with a spoon of honey stirring into her tea. Outside it was cold and grey, and she was dreaming of a sunny beach and a week of swimming. "Find me a hotel by the sea for four nights, starting next Friday," she told her phone. "I do not want a room on the ground floor, and I don't want anything near a busy road." The assistant asked how many people were going. "Just me," said Chiara. It searched and showed three hotels with sea-view rooms on high floors, all quiet. The cheapest one had a pool where she could swim every morning. Chiara picked it, and the assistant booked the room for four nights.

When you order food to your home, the app shows a time when it will arrive. Delivery is for days when you are too tired to cook. People often change small things about an order. They may say, put a label on the bag with my name, or leave the box on the floor by the door, or include a tip for the driver. If the food is late, people feel sad and ask, how long is my order going to take? They can also say, bring it to the back door, or make the tip bigger. The words are simple. The assistant reads them and changes the order.

Tyre pressure is a small number that matters. Each tyre needs the right amount of air. Too little air makes the car use more fuel and wears the tyres fast. Finding the right pressure can feel like a puzzle, but the sticker inside the driver's door tells you. A flat tyre on a road trip is a serious problem, so many drivers check often. People say, how much air does my front tyre need, or remind me to check the tyres on Sunday, or what is the pressure right now? When all four tyres are good, some drivers even celebrate with a short drive.

Jing was on a video call at work when her phone buzzed with a reminder about her doctor's appointment. She was muted and the meeting was going smooth, so she did not want to talk. She typed to her assistant, "Don't call the clinic. Just move my appointment to Thursday." The assistant said the clinic's page showed free times at nine and eleven. Jing wrote that she did not want the early one. The assistant picked eleven, changed the booking, and said the clinic is on Park Street, next to the bakery. When the manager asked her a question, Jing clicked to unmute and answered, and her day went on as before.

When you book a hotel room, you pick the night you arrive and how many nights you stay. Check-in is usually in the afternoon, and check-out is before noon. If you arrive early, you might wait an hour for your room. Many rooms have a kettle to boil water for tea, and some give breakfast to hungry guests. People change a booking by saying, make it three nights instead of two, one more guest is coming, or move my check-in to Friday. The hotel then changes the booking when you ask.

Sanne had just moved to the city in early autumn. Her fridge was nearly empty, and she wanted to enjoy a real dinner. She held up her phone and said, "Shopping list?" The assistant read out her list: eggs, rice and apples. "Bread," said Sanne. The assistant put bread on the list. Then she asked for the nearest shop. The assistant showed a small market two streets away, with a gold sign over the door, open until nine. Sanne put on her coat and went out.

Pavel owned a small shop and was proud of it. One evening the lights went out in the whole street. He found a pencil and a notepad by the till and asked his phone, "Help, how long will this power cut last?" The assistant checked the power company and said repairs would take about two hours, half as long as last month's cut. Pavel sighed and said, "Remind me in an hour to check the freezer." The assistant set the reminder. Then he asked for more light, and the assistant turned the phone's torch on and put it at full brightness.

A meal plan is a simple list of what you will eat each day this week. It helps you shop once and waste less food. Many people sort the plan by day: soup on Monday, rice on Tuesday, fish on Wednesday. They change it when life changes, for example when a child is sick and needs something light. People say things like swap Monday's dinner with Wednesday's, make the plan vegetarian, or I need packed lunches for five days. The assistant then changes the list and the shopping list too.

Abena was in a hurry. Her bus to the hills left in twenty minutes, and she zoomed around the flat looking for her bag. Her cart of laundry blocked the door. "Make me a packing list for a two-night camping trip," she told her phone. The assistant began with a tent, a sleeping bag and two pairs of socks. "No wait, three nights," said Abena. The assistant fixed the list, with a third pair of socks and more food. It also checked the most recent forecast and added a note: rain on Saturday, so pack a coat. Abena grabbed the coat and ran for the bus.

Chioma had just moved to the city and spent her first evening on the sofa with a book. The air in the flat was stale, so she opened a window. She wondered how long the book was. "Book length?" she asked her phone. The assistant said the book had three hundred and twelve pages, and she was on page ninety. "Bookmark page," she said, and the assistant saved her place. Then she asked, "Reading time?" It said that at her normal speed she would need about five hours to finish. Chioma decided to spend one hour each night.

Chidi was playing cook in the kitchen with his toy pans when his sister called, "It's so cold in here!" He looked at the radiator. It was off. "Make the living room twenty degrees," he told the voice assistant. The assistant set the heating to twenty and said the room would be warm in about thirty minutes. Chidi worried that he might break something. The assistant said no, the change was not permanent and he could change it again at any time. Chidi smiled, went back to his pans, and asked it to lower the heat at bedtime.

Chioma was a cook in a busy restaurant. A customer from Italy had walked a kilometer in the rain to find the place and wanted plain pasta, with no onions. Chioma did not know the words, so she wiped her hands and typed fast, "how do i say no onoins in italian". The assistant showed her the phrase, senza cipolle, and played the sound. Chioma said it out loud, and the customer laughed and clapped. The words sounded like a song, and Chioma began to sing them as she stirred the pot.

Mei was running late and felt nervous. The car engine was already running outside. She typed to her bank assistant, "move 200 from savings to chekcing, quick". The assistant moved two hundred dollars between her own accounts and said her checking balance was now four hundred and ten. Mei needed the money to load her bus card, because the car was for her brother. She thanked the assistant, grabbed her bag, and turned the engine off.

A contact is a card with a person's name, phone number and address. Your phone keeps these cards so you do not have to remember them. They lie in a list that you can search. People change them often. A friend moves, a number changes, or you want to put a birthday back on a card after you deleted it. You might say, change Sam's number to this one, save the address of my aunt, or save the number of the man who fixed my microwave. The assistant finds the right card and makes the change.

Chioma drove a taxi, and at dawn a wide grey sky hung over the city. Her customers would soon be waiting, and she had left her coat at home. She looked at her jeans, still damp from yesterday. "Looks like it's going to pour today, and I have no coat," she said to the car's assistant. The assistant understood she wanted the weather and said rain would fall until three, then it would be dry. It added that she should serve her first customers on the north side, where it was lighter. Chioma bought a cheap umbrella at the first stop.

Marlene, a busy parent, pushed a mop across the kitchen floor while her children made a paper craft at the table. The house felt hot, and last month's electricity bill had been huge. "Our bill is going to be crazy again," she said out loud. The assistant understood that she wanted to save energy. It showed her use for the day compared with normal, which was a lot higher. Then it suggested turning off lights in empty rooms. Marlene said yes, and the assistant turned off the living room lights and the old TV.

Jomar, a student, was moving out of his dorm. His boxes were dirty from the basement, and the movers would arrive at ten. "Movers' number?" he asked his phone. The assistant read out the number. "Call them," said Jomar. The assistant made the call, and the movers said they would arrive at ten fifteen instead. Then he asked, "Nearest shop?" The assistant showed a store three minutes away that sells packing tape, and Jomar ran to buy some.

Sanjay, a grandfather, was packing the car for a trip to see his grandchildren. "Which way is faster, the highway or the old road?" he asked. The assistant said the highway would take forty minutes and the old road double that, eighty minutes. The traffic on the highway was a mix of cars and trucks, but there were only a few jams. "Take me by the highway," said Sanjay. The assistant started directions and told him to leave in ten minutes. Sanjay put the last bag in the trunk and set off.

Nikola rounded the corner into her kitchen, tired after a night shift. "Make me a coffee, double strength," she told the coffee machine. The assistant started it and used twice the usual amount of coffee. Then Nikola asked for some soft music, and a quiet playlist began. Her phone showed an urgent text from the hospital: could she come at eight tonight? "Say yes," she told the assistant, and it sent the reply. Last, she asked for the music to be half as loud, and the assistant lowered it. Nikola sat down and drank her coffee.

An air purifier cleans the air in a room by pulling it through a filter. It is for people with allergies, dust, or smoke from outside, and bad air can be a serious problem for some of them. Note that a filter wears out, so people change it every few months. They also change the fan speed. People say, run the purifier on high, turn it down at night, how clean is the air right now, or open the window for fresh air. The assistant reads the request and changes the setting.

Tendai worked as a gardener and walked every morning before his shift. After a shower, he asked his phone, "Tell me how many steps I walked today." The assistant said he had walked three thousand steps and about two kilometers. "Set a goal of eight thousand steps," said Tendai. The assistant saved the goal and said it would remind him at lunchtime how many steps were left. Tendai smiled, put on his boots, and went out to water the beds.
